title: Deep learning points to MHC-I shielding mycosis fungoides cells from NK cells
summary: A clonality-supervised deep-learning analysis of mycosis fungoides identified the IL-32beta-MHC-I axis as a determinant of tumor T-cell immune evasion in skin. In patients' skin, MHC-I impaired natural killer cell function, reducing antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity. In female mice, disrupting the interaction between MHC-I and NK inhibitory Ly49 receptors restored NK anti-tumor activity and lymphoma elimination in vivo. Deep learning generated the hypothesis, and the in vivo work is in a mouse model.
ai_technology: Clonality-supervised deep learning on mycosis fungoides data to dissect pathological features
organization: Centre Hospitalier Universitaire Vaudois; University of Lausanne

evidence.tested: Patient skin analyses and murine in vivo experiments disrupting MHC-I and Ly49 interaction.
evidence.unknown: Clinical translation to patients; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Deep learning dissected pathological features and highlighted the IL-32beta-MHC-I axis.
